To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we introduce a differentiable Poisson solver for point clouds and demonstrate its use in learning-based shape reconstruction from unoriented points.

we present a differentiable point to mesh layer based on the Poisson Surface Reconstruction method, which enables us to efficiently represent 3D shapes as oriented point cloud, and that our approach is more interpretable and faster than other neural implicit and explicit 3D representations.
our differentiable Poisson solver can be used to accelerate the learning-based reconstruction of surfaces from point cloud data.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a differentiable Poisson solver that enables a differentiable and efficient point-to-mesh conversion, which in turn enables us to represent shapes in the form of point clouds, while preserving the advantages of neural implicit representations.

the following contributions: (a) a differentiable point to mesh layer using the PSR, (b) a novel explicit representation of shapes, Shape As Points (SAP), and (c) a new method for surface reconstruction from unorganized point clouds using SAP.
the development of a new representation that combines the best of both implicit and explicit representations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method, Shape-As- Points, represents shapes as oriented point cloud, which is explicit, lightweight, and expressive, and accelerates the inference time by one-order of magnitude.
SAP provides a new and promising representation for shape reconstruction and learning.
SAP can be used for both surface reconstruction from un-oriented point clouds and learning based reconstruction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our differentiable PSR point-to-mesh module enables a new way of representing 3D shapes as points.
we introduce Shape-As-Point (SAP) which is an explicit representation of shapes as oriented point sets, which is differentiable and can be trained end-to-end.

we propose a new differentiable layer to efficiently bridge explicit point representation and implicit indicator function, which allows us to represent 3D shapes as explicit points and enables end-to-end optimization for surface reconstruction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the point cloud is a flexible and expressive representation for 3D shapes, and we show that a differentiable point representation can be an effective alternative to neural implicit representations.
explicit 3D representations are still useful for learning-based reconstruction and can complement neural implicit representations.
we can achieve the best of both worlds: the flexibility and expressiveness of implicit neural representations and the efficiency and interpretability of explicit representations.
